Aja Monet: aja monet is a Surrealist Blues Poet in the business of goosebumps and heart-gut-telling truths. Her poems are harmolodic, vulnerable, and insurgent. As the youngest recipient of the Nuyorican Grand Slam Poetry title, she first cut her teeth in New York City’s Lower East Side poetry clubs and bars, honing her voice and craft on the storied stages of a burgeoning grassroots poetry movement. She follows in the long legacy and tradition of poets organizing in social movements for change. Her collaborative spirit has seen her shape and shift culture alongside internationally renowned artists, scholars, activists, and organizers. aja’s first full collection of poems, my mother was a freedom fighter (2017), is a powerful tribute to women who embody freedom, earning a nomination for a NAACP Image Award for Poetry. Her debut poetry album, when the poems do what they do , was nominated for a Grammy for Best Spoken Word Poetry Album in 2024. The album explores themes of resistance, love, and the inexhaustible quest for joy. As a poet and touring bandleader, she has performed at festivals, concert halls, and theaters across the globe including, but not limited to, the Guggenheim, Lincoln Center, Newport Jazz Festival, Montreal Jazz Festival, North Sea Jazz Festival, and the Fremantle Biennale, to name a few. As the 2025 Artist in Residence at the EFG London Jazz Festival, she was invited to give a headline performance at the Barbican Centre. aja monet’s awards include the Marjory Stoneman Douglas Award for Poetry (2019), the Nelson Mandela Changemaker Award (2024), the Harry Belafonte Voices for Social Justice Award (2024), the EBONY 100 Artist In Residence Award, and the Malcolm X & Dr. Betty Shabazz Vanguard Award (2025). She also serves as the Artistic Creative Director for V-Day, a global movement to end violence against women and girls. In 2022, she created VOICES , an audio play amplifying the stories of Black women across the diaspora and the African continent. aja monet’s most recent book of poems, inspired by several years living and organizing in South Florida, is called florida water on Haymarket Books.
Alex Intas: Alex Intas has been moving and shaking within the soulful underground for nearly two decades. Quietly going about his business, many might not know the magic touch Alex has had on bringing Australian music to the world or equally, bridging global influences to his native homeland. He joins the dots, and is commonly identified as an integral link in realising the vision. From his time up and down Australia’s east coast with notorious party purveyors Crown Ruler, A Love Supreme and now Astral People – to his work with Worldwide FM and Brownswood Recordings – Alex is a steward of music, well regarded for his wealth of knowledge, eclectic taste and passionate pursuit of promoting underground soul and club sounds. He’s curated compilations like Sunny Side Up, interviewed legends from Zapp to Kahil El’Zabar, written pieces for the likes of Stamp The Wax and Red Bull Music Academy – guided artists, rocked club nights, traded records and debated with the best of them. Alex is a critical piece of the puzzle. His latest foray Love High, formerly broadcast on Worldwide FM and now Naarm (Melbourne’s) Skylab Radio is a journey through “the musical marriage of a phat bottom and a pretty top”. Love High is unashamedly informed by a slicker underground soul of the 80s and 90s made up by silky voices, synth-bass lines and machine rhythms. Alex is recognised for digging deep and championing lost r&b obscurities and slept-on dollar bin pearls that kiss everything from quiet storm, new jack swing, street soul, g-funk, modern soul steppers, boogie funk and beyond.

His broadcasts are intimate and exploratory, often spotlighting overlooked records, deep cuts and new artists alongside timeless classics, all presented with a calm authority and deep respect for the music. As a DJ, Alexander Nut brings the same sensibility to clubs, festivals and listening spaces. His sets are patient, immersive and finely balanced, creating environments that reward attention and trust. Whether playing late night rooms or sunlit festival stages, his focus remains on building mood, space and emotional resonance. Respected for his taste, consistency and quiet influence, Alexander Nut continues to operate as a connector within the music community. Through radio, DJing and curation, he champions music as a shared experience, offering thoughtful alternatives to fast paced club culture and reaffirming the power of sound to bring people together. Amaro Freitas: In the sweltering North-Eastern Brazilian state of Pernambuco lies the coastal city of Recife, where Amaro Freitas is pioneering the new sound of Brazilian jazz. For the prodigious young pianist, the spirit of his hometown runs deep. From the Afro-Brazilian maracatu born on the sugar plantations of slavery, to the high intensity carnival rhythms of frevo and baião, Amaro’s heavily percussive approach to jazz is as indebted to these Pernambuco traditions as it is to Coltrane, Parker and Monk. As with many of the greats before him, Amaro began playing piano in church aged 12, under the instruction of his father, leader of the church band. As his natural talents became obvious, the young prodigy quickly outgrew his father’s instruction. He won a place at the prestigious Conservatório Pernambucano de Música but had to drop out as his family could not spare the money for the bus fare. Undeterred, Amaro gigged in bands at weddings and worked in a call centre to fund his tuition. The transformative moment came at age 15 when Amaro stumbled across a DVD of Chick Corea concert, “he completely blew my mind, I’d never seen anything like it but I knew that’s what I wanted to do with a piano”. Despite not actually owning a piano, Amaro devoted himself to studying day and night – he would practice on imaginary keys in his bedroom, until eventually striking a deal with a local restaurant to practice before opening hours. By the age of 22 Amaro was one of the most sought-after musicians in Recife and resident pianist at the legendary jazz bar Mingus. It was during this time he met and begun collaborating with bassist Jean Elton and the pair went in search of a drummer. “We kept hearing about this crazy kid who was playing in 7/8 or 6/4, we knew we had to meet him”. Hugo Medeiros joined, and the Amaro Freitas Trio was born.
Ana Frango Elétrico: Ana Frango Elétrico is a singer-songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, producer, and visual artist. Hailing from Rio de Janeiro’s vibrant independent scene, award-winning she is known for her genre-bending sound that defies easy labels. The result is a style that is both playful and sophisticated. Her spectacular concerts are wild and sensitive, showcasing music at the highest level. Anaiis: In a 1994 copy of Outlaw Culture: Resisting Representations, famed educator, author, theorist and activist bell hooks wrote: “The function of art is to do more than tell it like it is – it’s to imagine what is possible.” Her words speak to an innate sense of wonder, how truth is all too often stranger than fiction. While hook inks the meaning of art, French-Senegalese artist anaiis (whose name is in lowercase as tribute to hooks) translates that ethos into sound. On her forthcoming album Devotion & The Black Divine , the songs swell with emotional clarity and a growing sense of homecoming. Not to a place, but to the self. anaiis seems to be in conversation with the reverence of nature, recognising our own divinity, and therefore our wholeness in both chaos and beauty. She crafts a body of work that gently pushes herself (lovingly, as you’ll come to learn by listening through) to the edges of her comfort zone. New motherhood has been a core influence across the project. It deepened anaiis’ understanding of how to react with grace, create with freedom, and captures the reality of being human, unposed and unpredictable. That internal expansion is audible across the record. It leans into the idea that selfhood is something in motion; much like Octavia Butler’s reminder that “God is Change. Everything you touch you change, everything you change, changes you.” Like a tree shaped by its environment, growth isn’t always linear – there are knots and bends formed as it adapts to shifting climates. anaiis toys with this idea that the very nature of existence is to move fearlessly through what is unknowable. That search for freedom, in sound and in spirit, runs through every note. Where previous work offered catharsis and rupture, Devotion & The Black Divine draws strength from slowness and softness. It opens with “Something is Broken,” a track that lays past pain to rest and clears the ground for something more rooted to take shape. The album signals a deeper commitment to intuition and marks an ongoing transition that began during her time in Brazil, when a collaborative mini-album, anaiis & Grupo Cosmo , was created through live improvisation in just a week, with her newborn son in tow – marking a pivotal expansion in sound and approach. A string of recent releases have acted as prelude to this new chapter: a reimagining of Lauryn Hill’s “To Zion” performed at Chaka Khan’s Meltdown Festival, and two remixes of “B.P.E. (Black People Everywhere)” – a standout from the Brazil sessions – by Sango and Hagan, playlisted on BBC Radio 6 Music. Each release adds dimension to the whole, tracing a lineage of diasporic collaboration and cross-cultural kinship. Born in Toulouse, raised between Dublin, Dakar, Oakland, and now rooted in London, anaiis’ footholds have shaped a perspective founded in movement, flux, community and personal transformation. After her debut single “Nina” in 2018, anaiis released this is no longer a dream in 2021, featuring Chronixx, Sjava and Topaz Jones, with art direction by Ib Kamara and Rafael Pavarotti. She went on to support Daniel Caesar on his UK tour, share stages with Erykah Badu and Nick Hakim, headline a sold-out Barbican show, and speak at TEDxLondonWomen at the Southbank Centre. In 2025, she toured the US with Mereba and appeared at SXSW London. From a young age, anaiis was drawn to voice as a vessel for feeling, inspired by artists like Ella Fitzgerald, whose singing she likened to a nightingale, “a singer of infinite song,” speaking in a recent New York Times article. This early fascination grew into a broader creative lineage through the sacred work of Black thinkers and artists, not as echoes but as foundations that allowed her to explore her own voice. Nina Simone who cut through silence with urgent truth. Maya Angelou and James Baldwin who wrote from the depths of the soul’s undercurrents. Alice Walker’s spirited storytelling. Filmmakers like Ousmane Sembène who capture the nuances of resistance and identity. These influences shaped anaiis’ approach to creating with conviction, imagining with freedom and honouring curiosity as a compass. anaiis’ visual accompaniments to her music have long been an essential extension of her storytelling. Working closely with her partner Tayo Rapoport and detail-oriented collaborators like Ronan McKenzie, she builds out worlds through film to uncover an artform that invites us to sit between something that feels both fantastical and grounded all at once. Devotion & The Black Divine is soothing and spine-chilling at once, imbued with key messages of self-love. Rather than being defined by the past, anaiis moves towards something less contained and more aglow with possibility. Her voice stretches beyond its known range to seek out new qualities. On her new album, she speaks more about gratitude and acceptance than worry. An ongoing research on curbing the ego and the weight of fear. She captures the non-linear nature of healing and makes it feel beautiful through her tender lens.

Atjazz: Setting sail on a mammoth musical journey in 1995, soon followed by the release of his first recorded material in early 1996. Martin Iveson aka Atjazz has become known worldwide for his creativity and constant delivery of finely crafted music. Showing no signs of slowing, he continues to evolve sonically, stamping his unmistakable trademark wherever the journey takes him. From a misspent youth skateboarding the small towns of North-eastern England to running successful independent record labels, producing and remixing for artists across the globe, Atjazz has become synonymous with style, innovation and musical integrity within the independent dance-music world. After relocating to the Midlands in the early 1990s, Martin cut his teeth creating music and sound design for the then fledgling computer game developer Core Design Ltd . , contributing to numerous titles including the globally iconic Tomb Raider series. Alongside this work, any spare moment was devoted to developing his own deep, soulful and forward-thinking musical sound. Following 13 years at Core, Martin took the leap to focus fully on his artistic vision, founding Mantis Recordings as a platform for collaboration and experimentation. Early Atjazz releases such as Story , That Something and the seminal Labfunk established him as a deeply emotive and original force within the underground scene, steadily growing a loyal international following. As his reputation spread, Atjazz became a global presence behind the decks, leaving his mark at clubs and festivals worldwide. In recent years he has been embraced as family within the South African house-music community, earning the Best International Producer award at the Dance Music Awards South Africa. South Africa has since become his second home, where fans affectionately refer to him as “ Themba ” — meaning Hope in isiZulu. In 2009, following industry changes, Martin closed the chapter on Mantis Recordings and launched Atjazz Record Company (ARCo) , a diverse imprint focused on his productions and collaborations. This period marked renewed creative growth, further expanded in 2015 with the introduction of Less Than Ten , allowing him to experiment freely with new sounds and structures. Alongside his own labels, Martin continues close working relationships with Yoruba Records, R2 Records, Lazy Days, Foliage, and Reel People , while maintaining an extensive remix catalogue for artists including Nitin Sawhney, Bob Sinclar, Henri Mancini, Gilles Peterson’s ‘Havana Cultura’, Jazzanova, The RAH Band, Osunlade, Kerri Chandler, Omar and St Germain , among many others. A passionate collaborator and natural mentor, Atjazz has always loved working closely with other artists and helping new talent grow. This is perhaps best seen through his long-standing creative partnership with Jullian Gomes , with whom he released the much-loved albums The Gift The Curse and Big Bad Crazy . These projects capture a joyful meeting of generations and played a meaningful role in shaping the modern deep-house sound. Alongside this, Atjazz continues to support and mentor artists such as Si Tew, Sarai Jazz, South Beach Recycling and many others across his labels, always giving back to the community that has inspired him throughout his journey. Fans recognise that the Atjazz sound is deeply personal, with Martin pouring himself into every production. In recent years he has also released music under his given name, exploring a more introspective and unbounded creative space while retaining his signature warmth, groove and musical depth. In 2016, Martin celebrated 20 Years of Atjazz with a 3xCD retrospective compilation, including a re-release of his 1998 debut album That Something . Alongside his prolific studio output, Atjazz remains a world-class DJ, touring relentlessly and connecting with audiences across the globe.

In the tapestry of contemporary music, Bel Cobain stands as a beacon of authenticity. She channels the spirit of her influences while forging a path uniquely her own. BRYAN GEE (OLD SKOOL SET): Bryan Gee From the early days of rave to the present, he’s been an ever-present authority and tastemaker in drum ‘n’ bass, with an untestable deep collection of dubplates and grandmaster-level A&R skills. He started out in the seventies as a reggae sound system selector in his native Cheltenham, he eventually made his way to Brixton where he formed a deejaying partnership with Jumpin Jack Frost. As a champion of the emerging acid house sound, Bryan became well-known as a man with his finger on the pulse, earning him a job pushing the new rave-orientated music for the Rhythm King offshoot label Outer Rhythm. As jungle took over from hardcore, Bryan Gee linked up with Roni Size and Krust and a DnB institution was born, distinguished by that iconic sun-face logo and christened with the letter V. That “Bristol Sound” style of jungle drum ‘n’ bass that Bryan helped bring to the public went on to rack up awards, international success and critical acclaim, as well as inspiring a whole new generation of artists.

Channel One: Channel One Sound System is one of the UK’s best known and most loved reggae sound systems. Mikey took the name Channel One as homage to the legendary Channel One studio in Jamaica. In 1983, Channel One started playing at Notting Hill Carnival (check out video clip of Carnival 2018 in the hyperlink), they have played at Carnival every year since. Channel One is made up of selector Mikey Dread and MC Ras Kayleb. Channel One play a unique selection of conscious reggae, exclusive dubplates and uplifting steppas. Channel One’s hand built sound system provides a rich heavyweight bass sound, which compliments their tight selection of old and new roots music. Channel One’s mission is “to break down barriers via reggae music”, they have achieved this by travelling and playing to new audiences and venues all over the world. Charlie Dark: London based DJ, producer, poet and cultural force Charlie Dark has spent decades shaping the sound and spirit of UK underground culture. A founding member of Attica Blues, his journey began in the early 1990s at the intersection of hip hop, jazz, soul and spoken word, driven by a deep belief in music as a tool for connection, expression and community building. As Attica Blues, Charlie released two critically acclaimed albums that blended live instrumentation with forward thinking production and socially conscious lyricism, carving out a unique space in British music. Their collaborative debut as GENA (short for “God Energy, Naturally Amazing,” and loosely inspired by Gina from Martin), The Pleasure Is Yours, feels like a playful, soulful conversation between two kindred improvisers: Liv.e’s smoky, unpolished vocals glide through Riggins’ warm, percussive universe. Rooted in jazz, soul, and hip-hop as living language, the Dallas born Liv.e brings a raw, experimental approach to R&B, while Detroit native Riggins, known for his work with Common, Erykah Badu, The Roots, Madlib, and a close kinship with the late J Dilla. For both artists, GENA marks a natural evolution. Riggins whose rhythmic fingerprint has shaped the work of hip-hop and neo-soul legends continues his lifelong dialogue between jazz improvisation and beat science. Liv.e, following her acclaimed projects Couldn’t Wait to Tell You… and Girl in the Half Pearl, finds an exalted freedom in this space: her voice sounds like water, changing shape to fit the emotional container of each track on The Pleasure is Yours. Together they create a world that’s analog and ethereal , percussive and poetic, sonically bridging eras without ever settling in one.
Genevieve Namazzi: South-London raised bassist, Genevieve Namazzi, brings her quartet, ‘GENTET’ to the stage. Her performances captivate listeners, drawing them into her world of deep thought and reflection with upbeat grooves and heartfelt melodies. With influences stemming from modern jazz, modern classical, and from the East African diaspora, Genevieve’s compositions are fluid blends of genres and subject matters. From her debut in October 2025, to a lively performance at Brick Lane Jazz Festival 2026, Genevieve is looking forward to performing at We Out Here this summer!
Georgie Sweet: Georgie Sweet is a singer / songwriter currently based in Brighton, with a uniquely smooth, soulful vocal tone. An all-round creative soul, away from creating music, Georgie also works as an illustrator and animator. However, her lifelong love of music is unquestionable. She’s been a vocalist from a young age, initially working with her musical parents (a producer and professional singer respectively). Her own sound sits within the realm of glo-fi alternative r&b. From powerful piano-led ballads, to head-nod boom bap backdrops, this album exemplifies Georgie’s eclectic influences and unique talents as a writer and a vocalist, which are growing exponentially. Her sophomore album ‘I Swear To You’ received an abundance of praise from the likes of Jimmy Jam, DJ Jazzy Jeff, DJ Spinna, Bobbito, Gilles Peterson (including a live Worldwide FM session), Lauren Laverne (BBC 6 Music), Jamie Cullum (BBC Radio 2), Patrick Forge (NTS), Kev Beadle (Totally Wired), Clash Magazine, Somewhere Soul, Jazz FM, Rinse FM, Assorted Tapes (USA), Bandcamp ( ‘Albums of the Year ’) & many more. Currently signed to First Word Records , she collaborated with Children of Zeus on the title cut of their sophomore album, and has had remixes c/o Nu:Tone, Kaidi Tatham, Don Leisure & Last Nubian . As a live artist, she was hand-picked by Mahalia to perform at her “…Presents” series at The Jazz Cafe in London, and has also performed at Church of Sound, The Great Escape and Mostly Jazz festival , often performing with collaborative partner, Marc Rapson .
Giles Smith: Giles Smith has been a key figure and influential DJ at the forefront of deep, roots inspired dance music in London for 25 years. For 21 years before recently going solo, Giles was co-founder and one half of Secretsundaze. One of London’s most infamous, best loved and consistent parties and DJ duo’s. Giles has played at many of the best clubs across Europe, USA and Japan from Panorama Bar, Smart Bar, Giant Steps, Contact, Fabric, Robert Johnson to Closer. Known for his immaculate taste and his ability to blend soulful NYC / Chicago vocal cuts, raw Detroit inspired jams, broken beat, and boogie always sublimely programmed. In smaller, more intimate settings he sometimes leans into his love of street soul, hip hop and r&b. His DJ sets are characterised by a strong emphasis on groove and smooth flow, whilst never becoming too predictable. As a producer Giles was one half of respected production duo Two Armadillos from 2008 to 2013, before the tragic loss of his partner Martin Dawson. They released 16 EP’s as well as remixing the likes of Jovonn, Lana Del Ray, Commix and Leif. Since then, as 1 one half of Secretsundaze he released on world reknown labels such as Mule Musiq, Live at Robert Johnson and Phonica. Most recently in 2025 Giles has released on Eglo records and has a 2 nd release with the iconic label coming soon. Giles’s has a much loved, bi-monthly residency on NTS Radio and don’t forget to check his essential and epic deep dives for the stations “In Focus Series” on Ron Trent and Larry Heard. Im May 2025 Giles was invited to become a resident at one of London’s best new clubs, Number 90 Hideout with his “Giles Smith & Friends” party inviting the likes of Fred P, Volcov and Prosumer.
Gilles Peterson: Gilles Peterson is a broadcaster, DJ and record collector and We Out Here founder who’s played a pivotal role in supporting forward-thinking underground music in the UK and beyond over the past three decades. He hosts weekly primetime Saturday afternoon show on BBC Radio 6 Music that’s one of the broadcaster’s most popular music shows, helms independent record label Brownswood Recordings, and is the founder of online radio station Worldwide FM. Throughout his career, Peterson has promoted the new frontiers of jazz, hip-hop, and electronic music. He’s been recognised for his work with an MBE in 2004, an AIM Award for Indie Champion 2013, the Mixmag Award for Outstanding Contribution To Dance Music in 2013, the PRS for Music Award for Outstanding Contribution to Music Radio in 2014, and The A&R Award from The Music Producers Guild in 2019. Starting his career installing illicit transmitters and hosting shows for pirate radio station Radio Invicta, he later joined the newly-founded Jazz FM and, after that, joined the influential pirate-turned-legal station Kiss FM. In 1998, he was hired by BBC Radio 1, where he hosted a weekly show until his move to his current slot on BBC Radio 6 Music. He also hosts a syndicated radio program that is broadcast all over the globe, from Mexico City to Paris. He has been behind several game-changing record labels. Firstly, he founded Acid Jazz in the late eighties, and later he started Talkin’ Loud, whose roster included Incognito, Galliano, Young Disciples, Courtney Pine, MJ Cole, Terry Callier, The Roots, 4 Hero, Nuyorican Soul, Carl Craig’s Innerzone Orchestra and Roni Size’s Reprazent project. Five of the albums on Talkin Loud were nominated for a Mercury Prize, with Reprazent’s New Forms winning in 1997. His current venture, Brownswood Recordings, was formed in 2006 and has released Ghostpoet’s Mercury Prize-nominated debut album and the 2018 We Out Here project, a celebrated compilation showcasing the UK’s thriving young jazz scene. As a curator and collector, he’s compiled over 100 albums. In 2011, he founded the Steve Reid Foundation in memory of the legendary jazz drummer. The charity supports musicians who are ill and facing financial difficulties, with past recipients of support including Arthur Blythe, Bernie Worrell and George Cables. They’ve also partnered with the PRS for Music Foundation to create the Steve Reid InNOVAtion Award, which has supported upcoming artists such as Moses Boyd, Nubya Garcia and Sarathy Korwar. He curated the Look Up event series in 2018, which explored the arts and mental health and raised £20,000 for youth mental health charity Safaplace.
Glenn Underground: A true custodian of Chicago house culture, Glenn Underground is a producer and DJ whose sound is rooted in groove, soul and musical freedom. Emerging from Chicago’s rich lineage of house, jazz and gospel, Glenn has spent decades shaping a sound that feels both deeply classic and endlessly forward moving. His productions are warm, raw and human led, built around rolling basslines, live feeling keys and rhythms that invite dancers into a shared moment rather than a fixed destination. Whether behind the decks or in the studio, Glenn approaches music as a living conversation. His DJ sets unfold patiently, drawing from deep house, jazz funk and disco, creating spaces where dancers connect not just to the beat, but to each other. A longtime torchbearer for soulful dance music, Glenn Underground continues to remind us why Chicago house remains one of the most vital musical languages in the world.
Greentea Selecta: Greentea Selecta is the immersive DJ alter-ego and musical extension of British neo-soul adventurer Greentea Peng. Under the banner of Greentea Selecta, she curates hypnotic sound journeys drawn from her deep and eclectic vinyl and digital record collection, weaving soul, dub, reggae, psychedelic grooves, and left-field rhythms into late-night dancefloor sets that reflect her singular musical taste. More than a record spinner, Greentea Selecta is an expression of Peng’s expansive musical universe. Reflecting the same spiritual, soulful energy that defines her songwriting and performance, her DJ sets dive into immersive soundscapes, creating spaces where groove meets meditation and movement becomes ritual. Featured at major stages, from Rinse FM broadcasts to festival lineups, including performances at Glastonbury, Greentea Selecta brings her intuitive vibe and handpicked selections to audiences captivated by her genre-bending approach.
Greg Wilson: Greg Wilson is a Merseyside-based DJ who played a pivotal role in the development of UK club culture in the early eighties via his tenure at Wigan Pier and Manchester’s Legend, and also The Haçienda during its formative period, with his upfront selection of NYC electro-funk grooves. In 1983 he was the first DJ to mix live on UK TV. Taking a two-decade hiatus, during which time he produced the seminal ‘UK Electro’ compilation, plus acclaimed albums for UK hip hop pioneers the Ruthless Rap Assassins, he returned to DJing in 2003, connecting with a younger audience and taking his place at the forefront of the disco/re-edits movement, subsequently spreading his reach across the globe. His three ‘Credit To The Edit’ compilations did much to cement his reputation as did his now classic 2009 Radio One Essential Mix, one of 10 classics selected by the BBC to celebrate the first 500 mixes in the show’s history, and listed in 2015 by Rolling Stone magazine as one of the 25 greatest internet mixes of all-time, the same year in which he was presented with the DJ Mag’s Industry Icon Award. He is also a writer/commentator on dance music and popular culture, his Electrofunkroots archive and Being A DJ blogs becoming online touchstones whilst his 2020 book Discotheque Archives received widespread kudos, with a hardback edition published in 2023. Greg began DJing in 1975 and is regarded as one of the most important figures on the UK dance scene. He enjoyed hugely popular residencies in the early eighties at Wigan Pier and Manchester’s majorly influential Legend, having originally started out in his hometown, New Brighton. A pioneer of mixing in the UK, he became the first ‘dance music’ specialist hired for a regular weekly session at Manchester’s now legendary Haçienda club in 1983. Greg was instrumental in breaking the new electronic, post-disco records coming out of New York, a sound he has dubbed ‘electro-funk’. In 2003 he set up electrofunkroots, a website documenting this crucial era in the evolution of dance culture. Following a twenty year break, he returned to DJing and soon welcomed bookings throughout Europe and, subsequently, worldwide. Guedra Guedra: “DJ/Producer exploring tribal polyrhythms of the past and dancefloor music. Future Music from the Past.”
Handson Family: Local South London husband and wife team, Handson Family (Cyndi Anafo & Chris Ellis) have been DJing and promoting primarily independent music in the capital primarily for over two decades. Passionate about South London’s legacy of Black music club culture and the community they were raised in, HF have turned their hands to many creative ventures beyond DJing including sound creation, booking artists, client tailored events, running pop up spaces and social media content management.
Heléna Star: Heléna Star is one of the most exciting new DJ’s in the UK. A rising ‘Star’ in House and Techno, taking influences from the raw energy of it’s roots as well as soulful, bubbling baselines from across the globe. Star’s larger than life attitude can be felt within everything she does and you can catch her sharing her love of dance music across London, international venues, festivals or on her bi – m onthly residency on Foundation FM and now in New York with Half Moon.
HERBERT & MOMOKO: Matthew Herbert and drummer/ vocalist Momoko Gill release Clay via Strut in June 2025. A soulful, elastic collaboration, Clay treads nimbly between the dancefloor and the more introspective moods of the early hours, both reminiscent of Herbert’s iconic album Around The House while taking off in a compelling new direction. Agile and open-hearted, Clay is a thrilling, sonically adventurous record from two of the UK’s most forward-thinking artists. Orbiting around Herbert’s fleet-footed productions and the ingenuity of Momoko Gill’s dexterous, melodic writing, Clay is at once stripped-back and rhythmically complex, drawing on a variety of found sources – from japanese kotos to basketballs – to give the sound an unmistakably organic feel. Bringing together original sampling techniques, live improvisation and lush, expansive arrangements, Clay is lifted into higher realms by Momoko Gill’s intimate vocal performance, soaring wide-winged across the album’s eleven tracks, whether on the euphoric melancholia of ‘Mowing’ or the emotive duet ‘Heart’. Clay follows the 2024 release of debut collaboration ‘Fallen’ and Momoko Gill’s remix of Matthew Herbert’s ‘The Horse Is Here’. And yet, although Clay marks the first full-length release between Herbert and Gill, the duo’s shared passion for pushing sonic boundaries has played a crucial role in their respective careers to date. For Herbert that means treating the world as an instrument, making music using everything from the sounds of a bomb exploding in Libya, a horse skeleton, a tank driving over a meal made for Tony Blair, 20,000 dogs, 245 shops and countless other noises. His album ONE PIG – which follows the lifecycle of a pig from birth to plate – remains one of the most ambitious and provocative pieces of electronic music this century, cementing his reputation as an utterly singular composer, artist and producer. Self-taught in drums and composition, Momoko Gill’s journey to Clay has been similarly experimental – cutting her teeth in South London’s multi-disciplinary music scene, embracing new challenges and collaborating with the likes of Coby Sey, Tirzah and Alabaster DePlume. Although drums and vocals are her mediums of choice, Gill’s multi-instrumental talents were on full show on 2024’s EP as An Alien Called Harmony with poet/rapper Nadeem Din-Gabisi, and she continues to hone her style in the frictions between genres. With an intuitive feel for one another’s sound, Clay is a meeting of musical minds that resonates far beyond the sum of its parts – a startlingly fresh, beautifully conceived record from two artists who sound like they’ve been playing together all their lives.
Holly Reinhardt: Holly Reinhardt is a young aspiring bass player currently based in London, studying at the Royal Academy of Music. She initially made herself known through the support of Tomorrows Warriors, performing for them as part of Frontline from 2024-2025, and playing alongside other exciting talent on the London scene like Emily Tran and Laurie Rich. Her new sextet, as she steps up to the position as a band leader for the first time, is influenced by a multitude of genres and styles. Brian Blade and the Fellowship, Gerald Clayton, Trio Grande, Wayne Shorter and Classical influences like Bach and Messian are just a few of the key inspirations that contribute to her sound. The lineup consists of Ciarra Oswagu on flute, Alexander Sibley on alto saxophone, Anchit Sengputa on guitar, Angelica Coupland on piano, and Finlay McKenzie on drums.
HVYWGHT & THE OUTLOOK ORCHESTRA: The sound of Dubstep has evolved many times over the years following, and to celebrate the twenty year milestone of the sound, we have teamed up with London-based stalwarts HVYWGHT to present a debut performance by The Outlook Orchestra. If you missed them at Glastonbury last year, you’re in for a real treat. Expect a unique blend of bass music heritage and instrumental talent from young musicians from across the UK .– featuring SGT Pokes, Warrior Queen and Chunky & Live Dub mixing by V.I.V.E.K – closing out the Main Stage proceedings on Thursday!
Iko Chérie: Iko Chérie is the moniker of French multi-instrumentalist, singer and selector Marie Merlet. A resident at Total Refreshment Centre signed to Pingipung Records, she hosts Little Trouble Girls, a monthly radio show celebrating women in music, and moves between projects as both musician and DJ. You might have heard her playing psychedelic cumbia guitar with Malphino, performing on keys and percussion alongside post punk legend Gina Birch or singing on the latest Stereolab album. Her eclectic and carefully curated sets move through experimental gems, psychedelic grooves, ambient dub and underground leftfield electronics from around the world.
In Flames: Ruby & Josephine are In Flames. Born from the love of being true to yourself and DIY culture. In Flames hosted an eclectic radio show on NTS, created a club night at Vogue Fabrics and played for special events and festivals where they brought pure fire madness to the dance floor. They’re back together for WOH’26 so expect to contort yourself from the sounds of post-punk, post-funk and freaky disco. No rules. Pure fun.
Ivy Lab: Ivy Lab is a collaborative project between Sabre & Stray o riginally starting life as a trio, North London outfit Ivy Lab were brought together out of a shared enthusiasm for experimentations on the fringes of the UK bass music scene. The years that followed saw them go from strength to strength, earning a place in ‘The top 10 DJ’s of 2015’ (Mixmag) and propagating a new generation of hip-hop inspired abstractions housed within the framework of their ’20/20 LDN’ project. The duo now find themselves at the apex of the ‘Halftime’ / ‘Future Beats’ / movement – A motley assortment of actors from across the bass music landscape applying their sonic-heritage to experiments with hip-hop and drum machine electronica. Ivy Lab invested further in the exploration of this sound with the creation of their ‘20/20 LDN’ clubnight. Housed primarily at Brixton’s Phonox nightclub, it earned the characterisation of “ultra innovative” (Timeout Magazine) and a “London standout” (Mixmag).
James K: A version of James K was born. Comprised of bones, reactive metals, and a larynx with freckled eyes that catalyzes that mix, she can now see through all the schemes. This is the truth. When she chews gum, it’s not clear which one of her personas does it. Since their first release in 2013, describing them separately is grunt work, as they switch places, cosplay each other, and would most likely lull you into a lonesome dream. Together, they know how to produce, sound, film, and edit. Thus, they are brought to the table, performing and DJing in clubs and theaters, alongside composers and children alike. She has performed in festivals and venues such as Dekmantel, Sustain Release, Mutek, iii Points, and Nowadays. In recent years, she has shared the stage with James Ferraro, Robert Aiki Aubrey Lowe, Yves Tumor, Morton Subotnick, Nick Leon, and Priori, among many others. She has released with labels such as AD 93, Incienso, PAN, iDEAL, Dial, and UNO, among others, and started her label She Rocks! in 2015. Her collaboration with hoodie, a 10” titled Scorpio , was released in summer 2023 via AD 93, landing on numerous EOTY lists. She followed up with another single, the trip-hop gem Blinkmoth (July Mix) , which has garnered similar attention—landing at number 2 on Resident Advisor’s Best Tracks of 2024 and numerous other EOY lists, the former publication naming her Producer of the Year. K has been a resident on NTS with her show Trip Lick since 2019, and she has provided mixes for series such as Dekmantel, Crack, and Fact. She is sought after for her signature magnetic vocals, lyricism, and production, and through collaborations has created critically acclaimed music with artists such as Moin, Fergus Jones + Huerco S., Priori, Special Guest DJ, Yves Tumor, Drew McDowall, LEYA, and many others. She produces music that makes temporary haven for indomitable lyrics—and these are in constant flux. You can check what they are here: [917 908-1173]. It’s only a part of her fairly detailed world. A world that she abandons and then builds upon. Take a sip of water before your memory error blinks. Dial to K. Listen to the disfragmented territory and the cast she’s making. It might not be what you will have thought tomorrow.
Jamie Woon: A cult artist and London soul pioneer with cosigns from Erykah Badu and Pharrell, Jamie has collaborated with Burial and Disclosure, written and produced for Elmiene, and built a devoted following on songs like Night Air and Sharpness. Now he’s back. For anyone who waited: these shows are for you. He is a distinctive voice in British music, rhythms that sit deep in the body, songs that don’t look away.
Jamz Supernova: Jamz Supernova uses sonics to tell a story. The multi-faceted creative force is a label head, radio host, DJ, podcaster, and true tastemaker, broadcasting for over a decade. Known for selecting sounds that span musical genres and subcultures, what she enjoys is the intimacy of sharing music with her community over radio. Her award-winning Saturday daytime show on BBC 6 Music is where she sits in as a storyteller, exploring global communities and unearthing exciting scenes through platforming underground music that rarely graces the mainstream. Outside of radio, Jamz heads up seminal label Future Bounce working in both an A&Ring and consulting capacity. The label’s 5 year anniversary in 2023 ended with a nomination at the DJ Mag Best of British Awards. Through her vibrant DJ sets, Jamz is a mainstay at festivals and clubs worldwide, spinning an eclectic mix of broken beat, UK funky, Bass, techno and beyond at the likes of We Out Here Festival, Worldwide Sete, All Points East and more. Having also hosted her own podcast series DIY Handbook & Between The Lines, plus television shows for BBC Three, FOUR & Newsbeat, and music awards ceremonies – including the prestigious Mercury Prize – for Jamz, the possibilities are endless. But Jamz will continue to rise by doing what’s always worked for her – staying true to herself, and to those that resonate with her craft.
Jazzanova (Live): Formed in the late 1990s in Berlin, Jazzanova quickly established themselves as architects of a genre-defying sound that fused the improvisational spirit of jazz with the textures of electronic music, global rhythms, and leftfield soul. As producers, DJs, and curators, the collective—comprised of Alexander Barck, Claas Brieler, Jürgen von Knoblauch, Stefan Leisering, and Axel Reinemer—played a pivotal role in shaping the nu-jazz and broken beat movements of the early 2000s. Their 2002 debut album In Between was a landmark release, blending live instrumentation with intricate sampling and forward-thinking production. Featuring collaborators like Clara Hill, Vikter Duplaix, Capitol A, and Ursula Rucker, the record redefined what jazz could sound like in the 21st century—bridging club culture and live performance with rare elegance and precision. In 2025, Jazzanova marked the album’s enduring legacy with In Between (Deluxe Edition) —a five-part anthology that spans the original album, a live reinterpretation ( In Between Revisited ), two volumes of remixes by a new generation of global producers, and a rare collection of pre-album singles. Together, the collection affirms In Between’s impact on the evolution of electronic jazz, while highlighting its continued relevance in today’s musical landscape. Beyond their own releases, Jazzanova’s influence has rippled outward through countless remixes, their cult-favorite label Sonar Kollektiv, and their work as tastemaking DJs and radio hosts. They’ve remixed artists from Common and Lenny Kravitz to Calexico and Fat Freddy’s Drop, always with a sharp ear for groove and harmonic depth. In recent years, the group has entered a new phase—balancing reinvention and reflection, honoring the past while charting new sonic territory. The Pool (2018) introduced a new generation of collaborators, while their Live at Little Big Beat Studios recordings and remix projects celebrate the elasticity and continued vitality of their sound. At their core, Jazzanova remain sonic explorers—equally rooted in jazz tradition and electronic innovation, always seeking the space in between.
JKriv: JKriv is a Brooklyn-based producer, DJ, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, and labelowner. Widely known as a co-founder of labelRazor-N-Tape, J is also a highlyrespected producer, prolific remixer, and DJ. In a music career stretching 2 decades, JKriv has blazed an unconventional paththrough club world, beginning as a trained jazz musician and live performer beforehoning his studio and DJ skills. JKriv’s prolific production work has yielded scoresof releases onRazor-N-Tape,SoundwayRecords ,Heist Recordings,MotonRecords,ZRecords, and many other labels. As a songwriter, arranger, collaborator, and studio musician, J has worked with luminary artistsDimitriFromParis,HorseMeatDisco feat. KathySledge,AdiOasis,JohnMorales,DamesBrownand many more. JKriv’s music has garnered support from all quarters ofclub and radio DJs, such as Gilles Peterson, Antal, Hunee,Colleen“Cosmo”Murphy,DerrickCarter,Disclosure,AndrewWeatherall,LouieVega,KennyDope,CraigCharles,andJamzSupernova, to name a few.J dropped loads of music in 2025, including his Intuition EPon Razor-N-Tape, theAdaptationEPon Rocksteady Disco, an exclusive song on Quantic’sK7D JKicks compilation, and remixes onUbiquity,WahWah45s,LumberjacksinHell,JulietRecords. JKriv’s 2026 release schedule includes collaborations with keyboardist Jason Lindner and Peter Matson respectively on Razor-N-Tape and Favorite Recordings, a track on aMake-A-Dance12” comp, numerous remixes nd a full length live album fromAJoyfulNoise, a project produced musical directed by J documenting 3 years of events at Brooklyn clubPublicRecords.As co-founder of Brooklyn labelRazor-N-Tape, JKriv has had a sizable impact on both the local NY and global dance music scenes. The label’s prolific andconsistent quality output across 150+releases over 12 years of operation hasearned them eminent respect and support from club DJs, radio selectors andlisteners around the world. The Razor-N-Tape Brooklyn shop, now in its 4th year ofoperation, is an established community hub for the local dance music scene.A resident onTheLotRadio, JKriv’s DJ sets showcase his deep and diverse taste,weaving eclectic disco, house, world grooves, and offbeat selections togetherseamlessly. J has also recently been a featured guests onNTSRadio,OpenlabIbiza,BalamiiRadioand hosted his own regular “Living Sounds” show on RadioAlhara throughout lockdown.With a busy stateside touring schedule in early 2026 including Dante’sHifi( Miami),MadRadio( NYC & Miami),PublicRecords, Mustache Bash(San Diego),Groovewell Vacation(California), this summer JKriv will be returning to GillesPeterson’sWeOutHerefestival for the second time along with numerous otherUK/EU dates.
Jobsearch: Jobsearch is a London-based pop and jazz fusion band led by Eliza Dunhill. Blending original singer-songwriter material and funk-inspired instrumentals, the band draws inspiration from artists such as Stevie Wonder, Blue Mitchell and Daft Punk. With a brass-heavy sound, strong horn arrangements and lively improvisation, Jobsearch brings an energetic live show to We Out Here guaranteed to get audiences moving!
John Glacier: London-based rapper, poet and producerJohn Glacier creates boundary-pushing blended musical styles that, partnered with her personal and rawly delivered narrative, radiate a deeply emotive quality. It’s this captivating authenticity that draws you into her introspective world.
Joy Crookes: Joy Crookes is a British singer-songwriter from South London known for her rich, soulful voice and sharp, socially aware songwriting. Blending soul, jazz, R&B, and pop, her music often explores identity, politics, and love with wit and emotional depth. She broke through with a run of acclaimed EPs before releasing her debut album Skin , which cemented her as one of the UK’s most distinctive new voices.
KAMAR: Palestinian, Lebanese and British Kamar is a DJ and record collector, uncovering dance music of the global diaspora. Kamar’s name, based on the Arabic ‘Qamar’, which means moonlight, reflects his heritage and the feeling that many places have felt like home. His life’s experience has seen him travel extensively with an ethnomusicological focus across Latin America, the Middle East and South Asia, as well as live in Cape Town and Lisbon. Join Kamar on the WOH Radio stage for “Tealeaves: Exploring South African Musicians Exiled Under Apartheid Rule”. This show will explore the powerful legacy of South African musicians who were exiled under apartheid’s brutality yet kept their homeland’s spirit alive through extraordinary innovations, particularly in Jazz – our presenter, Kamar, host of Tealeaves on Worldwide FM, will delve into the lives and compositions of artists like Hugh Masekela, Miriam Makeba, and Abdullah Ibrahim, and more, whose music became both refuge and resistance.
KASSA GJ QUARTET: Kassa GJ Kassa Green-Jakcsi is a talented 17-year-old alto saxophonist from London, currently studying at the Guildhall School of Music. Born and raised in Hackney, he began taking saxophone lessons at the age of 8. Inspired by the likes of Kenny Garrett, Immanuel Wilkins, and Herbie Hancock, Kassa’s growing reputation as an innovative composer with a powerful approach to improvisation has already got many in the London jazz scene anticipating an exciting musical journey ahead. He joined the acclaimed Tomorrow’s Warriors Young Artist Development Programme at the age of 14, where he has gained experience playing in their Youth Ensemble and Nu Civilisation Orchestra. Currently mentored by Gary Crosby, Binker Golding, and Denys Baptiste, he has had the privilege of performing at Dizzy’s Club in New York, the Barbican, and the Southbank Centre, as well as Love Supreme and We Out Here festivals.
Kay Suzuki: Japan-born and London-based since 2004, Kay Suzuki is a music producer whose releases have earned support from David Mancuso, Gilles Peterson, DJ Harvey, François Kevorkian, Theo Parrish, Laurent Garnier and Bradley Zero. From 2013 to 2016 he was a founding member and Head Chef of Brilliant Corners in East London, where he helped establish the venue’s early identity. In 2018 he launched Time Capsule, a record label reissuing overlooked music from across the globe. Its catalogue spans Italian New Age, Brazilian funk, South Indian classical, French Caribbean rhythms and Japanese fusion. The 2024–25 Nippon Series drew coverage from Pitchfork, The Wire, BBC and NTS. Suzuki has also hosted regular shows on NTS and Worldwide FM, and is frequently invited to DJ across Europe and Asia. His sets are not genre exercises but explorations of rhythm and time — tracing connections across cultures and creating shifts in perception that mirror his wider practice as a producer and curator. Since 2023 he has led the Tokyo Riddim Band, an intergenerational Japanese reggae project that has sold out London shows, appeared at The Jazz Cafe, and is touring internationally in 2025–26.
King Britt: Philadelphia-born Pew Fellow King James Britt (his given name) is a producer, composer, performer, and Full Teaching Professor of Computer Music at the University of California San Diego, where he integrates three decades of professional practice into a curriculum focused on contemporary electronic music, creative research, and culturally engaged pedagogy. His work emphasizes non linear approaches to technology, improvisation, and Black musical innovation, shaping new models of electronic music education. As a composer and producer, he has collaborated with De La Soul, Madlib, Kathy Sledge, and directors Michael Mann & Khalil Joseph , and has been commissioned to remix artists including Miles Davis, James Brown, Solange, and Calvin Harris | Dua Lipa. He recently released a studio project with MacArthur Fellow and Pulitzer Prize winner, Tyshawn Sorey. A globally active performer, he has appeared at AfroPunk, Berghain, MoogFest, and Le Guess Who, and was the original DJ for the Grammy-winning Digable Planets. He also created the groundbreaking course & festival, Blacktronika, Afrofuturism in Electronic Music that honors the innovators of color in electronic music that have been overlooked within the historical narrative. Guests in the class have included Herbie Hancock, Questlove, Patrice Rushen and many more. Expanding Charlie Dark’s original Blacktronika forward.
Klara Devlin: Those in the know are already excited about the rise of trumpeter Klara Devlin on the British jazz scene. Nightmares On Wax: UK electronic music project Nightmares On Wax , led by producer and DJ George Evelyn, has been a consistent and evolving presence in underground music since the early 1990s. After early releases on Warp Records, Nightmares On Wax became known for albums that favoured mood, groove and atmosphere over rigid genre boundaries. Records such as Smoker’s Delight and Carboot Soul helped establish a template for downtempo and leftfield electronic music that centred feeling, musicality and everyday experience, resonating far beyond the club. At the core of the project is a strong sense of rhythm and space, drawing equally from soundsystem culture, sample based hip hop and live instrumentation. Over the years, Nightmares On Wax has collaborated with a wide range of vocalists and musicians, allowing the sound to remain fluid while retaining a clear identity rooted in groove and intention. As a DJ and live performer, George Evelyn brings this same sensibility to the dancefloor, moving between downtempo, house, disco and soulful electronic music with a focus on flow and connection. Whether in clubs, festivals or listening spaces, his sets reflect a lifetime of musical exploration and an instinctive understanding of how sound shapes shared experience. Through decades of releases, performances and quiet influence, Nightmares On Wax continues to operate as a bridge between scenes, eras and communities, offering music that invites people to slow down, tune in and move together. Peven Everett: Peven Everett is an artist, multi-instrumentalist, and vocalist born in Harvey, Illinois, just outside Chicago, into a musical family. From an early age, he showed a natural connection to music—first by playing everyday objects as instruments, and soon after receiving his first drum kit from his mother. During school, he studied music under Sherman, John Weber, and David Eanes, quickly standing out as a dedicated and skilled musician. He held first chair positions across multiple instruments and also spent time student-teaching younger peers. While still young, he performed alongside legendary artists including Dizzy Gillespie and Betty Carter. At seventeen, after earning a perfect score on his exam at the Merit Carl Fischer Music Academy, Peven was awarded a full scholarship to Berklee College of Music. Around this time, he played his first professional performance at Carnegie Hall and soon moved to New York to join Betty Carter. He served not only as a performer but also as her music director, leading and working with musicians older than himself. While in New York, he collaborated with Wynton Marsalis and appeared in the documentary Marsalis on Music , as well as the accompanying book. He also toured with Buckshot LeFonque, Branford Marsalis’s band. During this period, he was featured in The New York Times Magazine in an article titled “The Next Miles Davis May Be On This Page,” written by Stephen J. Dubner. After his time in New York, Peven focused on composing and producing his own music, drawing on his ability to play over thirteen instruments. One of his early compositions, “Gabrielle,” created with longtime bandmate Frank Parker Jr., gained recognition and was later featured in the Alvin Ailey production Grace . The track helped bring wider attention to his work, earning coverage from publications including Straight No Chaser , Time Out , and Vibe , and radio play on BBC Radio 1 with Gilles Peterson. “Gabrielle” is also associated with the emergence of the Two Step genre. Peven has continued to create and release music consistently, with projects including Studio Confession , Latest Craze , Kissing Game , Easy Living , and Power Soul . Alongside these, he has independently released a large body of work, often sharing music directly with his audience to build a close and lasting connection. His catalog now includes well over 50 albums’ worth of material. In 2006, he received the Heineken Red Star Soul Independent Achiever Award. He has also performed in tribute concerts honoring Prince and Stevie Wonder. Known for his live performances, Peven has appeared on television programs including Late Night with Carson Daly , as well as broadcasts on NBC and WGN. He has been featured in interviews with international DJs and hosts, including Garth Trinidad on KCRW. In 2008, he was voted Best R&B Artist in Chicago by readers of the Chicago Reader . With a career built on consistent creativity and musicianship, Peven Everett continues to make music and share it with an audience that has grown steadily over time.
Plumm: Plumm is a South London-based vocalist, composer, multi-instrumentalist, and bandleader with a Welsh core, creating a sound that sits at the intersection of trip-hop, alternative electronica, and the UK’s evolving jazz underground. Her self-released track You Are The One (Live) features as the title track for the Apple TV series Liaison , marking a significant crossover into screen and international audiences. Plumm’s music is dark, ethereal, and vocal-led—blending improvisation with electronic textures and anthemic songwriting. Drawing inspiration from Cocteau Twins, Massive Attack and Björk. Her vocal sample pack GarageVol.1 is also out now, expanding her creative output into production and sound design.
Poly-Ritmo: Poly Ritmo is a London based DJ, musician, broadcaster and curator bringing heat to the hips and feet with vibrant selections from around the globe. A devoted collector and crate digger, her passion for telling stories through music began at age ten, when she started making mixtapes for friends and family. That spark grew into a lifelong passion for sharing music, one that took root while working at the iconic Sounds of the Universe record shop. Driven to dig deeper, she went on to study Ethnomusicology at SOAS, nurturing a nuanced, research driven approach to her craft. This deep knowledge shines through her DJ sets, where her selections are soulful, percussive and eclectic, often including zouk, Brazilian boogie, broken beat, soukous, salsa, disco and soca. Poly Ritmo has played at iconic festivals and venues such as Rio Carnival, Glastonbury, Giant Steps, GALA, We Out Here and Magnetic Fields. She’s also toured India, Brazil, Europe and Australia, as well as playing sets in Egypt, Turkey, Tunisia, Albania, Ibiza and Thailand. She made her Boiler Room debut in 2020, hosting a Brazilian session with live performances from Marcos Valle, Sabrina and Alex Malheiros, Ivan Conti and Kassin. A beloved presence in the radio world, Poly Ritmo has hosted shows on Worldwide FM, NTS, Foundation FM and Na Manteiga, and her My Analog Journal mixes have racked up millions of views. Beyond the decks, she co founded the much celebrated Basket of Light festival, a three day music and arts gathering featuring live music, DJs, workshops, theatre and lighting installations, now in its fourth year.
RE:NI: re:ni is the alias of Lauren Reni Bush, a DJ & producer based in South East London. Ri Mistry: Ri Mistry is an emphatically London-based DJ. She also throws nights with Social Records Society, using the platform to spotlight DJs she backs and fulfil her passion for record digging and community.
Rikette Genesis: Riketté Genesis’s DJ selections are a soulful tapestry woven from her deep love for vinyl culture and her eclectic musical influences. As a reggae selector and host of a monthly show on Voices Radio, she curates all-vinyl sets that traverse the rich landscapes of reggae, Ethiopian jazz, and soul. Her selections are not just about playing records; they are about telling stories and creating atmospheres that resonate with listeners. Born to a reggae backing vocalist mother and a devout Rastafarian father, Riketté’s upbringing was steeped in the rich musical traditions of Jamaica. This heritage profoundly influences her musical identity and selection style. Her father, who has since passed away, instilled in her a deep appreciation for reggae music and its cultural significance. This foundation is evident in her performances, where she often honors reggae legends like Burning Spear, Tommy McCook, and Keith Hudson, weaving their timeless sounds into her sets.
Roberta Cutolo: Born in Bari and spiritually formed in London, Roberta’s path has never been about career — it has been about calling. For over three decades she has moved through London’s underground not as a spectator, but as a custodian of feeling. From the early days around Dingwalls and Bar Rumba’s That’s How It Is to the extended family of Straight No Chaser, she gravitated toward spaces where music meant more than entertainment — where it was conversation, education, elevation. Her introduction to David Mancuso and the philosophy behind The Loft marked a quiet but permanent shift. Sound was no longer just selection — it was intention. The room became an organism. The DJ became the host. The dancefloor became a sanctuary. That ethos continues to guide her. Whether on radio — with her monthly transmissions on TWR and guest appearances on Soho Radio — or in listening spaces such as Spiritland, Brilliant Corners, Caia, Bambi , NDR Rec, New Forms, 180 The Strand, 360 Netil, Café 1001, Hackney Grow, Jago, Brixton Village Roberta approaches music as a form of stewardship. She builds patiently. She leaves space. She trusts the arc. Her sets are not designed to dominate a room, but to align it. Frequencies unfold with care — jazz spirituals into Brazilian pulse, broken rhythm into deep soul, moments of stillness into collective lift. Vinyl or digital is secondary; vibration is primary. Behind the decks and behind the scenes, the same sensitivity guides her curatorial work — from shaping Flora Purim’s long-awaited return on Strut Records to crafting archival journeys with BBE Records alongside Paul Bradshaw. These projects speak to lineage — honouring elders while keeping the continuum alive. Roberta understands that a dancefloor, at its best, is a temporary community built on trust. Lights low. Sound warm. Barriers softened. Strangers moving as one. She plays for that moment — when time dissolves, when connection feels effortless, when the music seems to breathe on its own. Not performance. Presence. Not hype. Frequency. Music as an offering. Music as memory. Music as home. #musicislife

SALUTE: Vienna by way of Manchester DJ and producer salute has emerged as one of the most distinctive voices in contemporary club music, blending emotional songwriting with a deep understanding of UK dancefloor culture. Drawing from garage, grime, dubstep and house, their sound balances warmth, momentum and melody, shaped by years spent immersed in clubs, radio and community led spaces. salute was first initiated into the UK club scene at 18 after moving to Brighton and later Manchester, where early exposure to club culture helped refine their approach as both a DJ and producer. What began as an exploration inspired by online sets and Boiler Room videos quickly evolved into a hands on understanding of sound system energy, crowd dynamics and genre fluidity. In 2024, salute announced their forthcoming album TRUE MAGIC , due July 12th on Ninja Tune. As a DJ, salute is known for expressive, high energy sets that move fluidly between genres while maintaining a strong emotional throughline. Their live catalogue includes performances at Coachella’s Do Lab, Boiler Room Melbourne, multiple appearances at Glastonbury, a BBC Radio 1 Essential Mix live with Annie Mac and The Blessed Madonna, and international shows across Europe, Asia and the US. With a 2024 MOBO Award nomination for Best Electronic or Dance Act and a growing global presence, salute continues to build a body of work rooted in connection, collaboration and the shared experience of the dancefloor. Santa Leticia: Rooted in the sun-kissed lands of Andalusia and now based in Newcastle, Santa Leticia pieces together soulful, percussive journeys across Latin America, the Caribbean, and Africa. A tribute to the obscured and the uncelebrated, this show brings forgotten rhythms into the light, warm, raw, and full of history
Sarah Love: DJ Sarah Love is a veteran club DJ, radio broadcaster, presenter, performer and journalist who has performed in over 30 countries. She’s shared stages with DJ icons like Grandmaster Flash and Jazzy Jeff , and supported artists including Mary J Blige , Wu-Tang Clan and The Roots . Sarah was headhunted by BBC Radio to present the 1Xtra Friday Night Hip Hop Mix Show and the Weekend Wake-Up Show , receiving global prestige as one of the few female specialists in worldwide broadcasting. MTV Europe appointed Sarah their official — and only — female VJ for the MTV Base Network , broadcasting to over 60 countries worldwide, interviewing stars for MTV: The Lick , NFL Touchdown.
